From 41c606879f89623dd5269eaffea640b915e9e17c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2022 17:43:39 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown"

This reverts commit 927728a34f11b5a27f4610bdb7068317d6fdc72a.

Once the uart_port->rs485->flag is set to SER_RS485_ENABLED, the port
should always work in RS485 mode. If users want the port to leave
RS485 mode, they need to call ioctl() to clear SER_RS485_ENABLED.

So here we shouldn't clear the RS485 bits in the shutdown().

Fixes: 927728a34f11 ("serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown")
Signed-off-by: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220418094339.678144-1-hui.wang@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c b/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
index e857fb61efbf..5fb201c1b563 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
@@ -1238,12 +1238,10 @@ static void sc16is7xx_shutdown(struct uart_port *port)
 
 	/* Disable all interrupts */
 	sc16is7xx_port_write(port, SC16IS7XX_IER_REG, 0);
-	/* Disable TX/RX, clear auto RS485 and RTS invert */
+	/* Disable TX/RX */
 	sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
+			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c`**
   - The `sc16is7xx_shutdown` function has been modified to remove the clearing of RS485-related bits during the shutdown process.
   - Specifically, the lines that cleared the `SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT` and `SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT` have been removed. The function now only disables TX and RX without affecting the RS485 configuration.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The patch is a revert of a previous commit (927728a34f11) that introduced the clearing of RS485 bits in the shutdown function. The rationale for this revert is that once the RS485 mode is enabled, it should remain active until explicitly disabled by the user through an ioctl call. Thus, the relationship is that the current patch undoes the changes made by the previous commit to maintain the intended behavior of the RS485 mode in the driver.

Revert "serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown"

This reverts commit 927728a34f11b5a27f4610bdb7068317d6fdc72a.

Once the uart_port->rs485->flag is set to SER_RS485_ENABLED, the port
should always work in RS485 mode. If users want the port to leave
RS485 mode, they need to call ioctl() to clear SER_RS485_ENABLED.

So here we shouldn't clear the RS485 bits in the shutdown().

Fixes: 927728a34f11 ("serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown")
Signed-off-by: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220418094339.678144-1-hui.wang@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the RS485 mode during the shutdown process of the serial driver. The previous implementation cleared the RS485 configuration bits, which led to the port not retaining its RS485 mode when it should have. This behavior contradicted the expectation that once RS485 mode is enabled, it should remain active until explicitly disabled by the user.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void sc16is7xx_shutdown(struct uart_port *port)
 {
 	struct sc16is7xx_port *s = dev_get_drvdata(port->dev);
 	struct sc16is7xx_one *one = to_sc16is7xx_one(port, port);
 
 	kthread_cancel_delayed_work_sync(&one->ms_work);
 
 	/* Disable all interrupts */
 	sc16is7xx_port_write(port, SC16IS7XX_IER_REG, 0);
-	/* Disable TX/RX, clear auto RS485 and RTS invert */
+	/* Disable TX/RX */
 	sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
+			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
 
 	sc16is7xx_power(port, 0);
 
 	kthread_flush_worker(&s->kworker);
 }

```c

                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
                      ...
```
Reason:
The code incorrectly clears the RS485 configuration bits during the shutdown process, which causes the port to exit RS485 mode unexpectedly. This contradicts the expected behavior that once RS485 mode is enabled, it should remain active until explicitly disabled by the user.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
// Removed clearing of RS485 bits
// sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
//                       SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |

```
Reason:
By removing the clearing of the RS485 bits in the shutdown function, the port retains its RS485 mode as intended. This ensures that the RS485 configuration remains active until the user explicitly disables it through an ioctl() call, aligning the behavior with user expectations.
